channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan's foreign trade turnover reached $49.5 billion in seven months
item.description: Uzbekistan's foreign trade turnover for January-July 2026 reached $49.5 billion, an increase of $3.7 billion or 8.1% compared to the same period last year. Imports of machinery and transport equipment were $9.7 billion, while exports of goods, excluding gold, increased by 27.7%.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Reduce Unified Customs Duty for Individuals from June 2027
item.description: From June 1, 2027, Uzbekistan will reduce the unified customs duty for individuals importing goods for non-commercial purposes. If the calculated duty is less than the required fees, these fees will not be collected.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan traffic police return to regions after SCO summit
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Interior Minister thanked traffic police for their service during the SCO summit. The head of the traffic police conveyed the minister's gratitude to the personnel. Officers ensured road safety and traffic flow during the international event and are now returning to their regions to resume normal duties.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Pakistan sign 16 bilateral documents to boost cooperation
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and Pakistani Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif signed 16 documents expanding cooperation in trade, transit, security, education, and healthcare. Agreements include transit trade, extradition, and mutual legal assistance. Joint projects are planned in pharmaceuticals, agriculture, energy, and tourism, aiming for practical partnership.

item.title: Kazakhstan dismantles international drug network recruitment channel
item.description: Kazakhstan's Interior Ministry reported a large-scale operation dismantled an international channel recruiting people into a drug network. The year-long operation, involving Ukraine, Albania, Interpol, and the US, uncovered call centers and identified organizers. Suspects promised easy money but involved individuals in international drug trafficking.

item.title: Uzbekistan Expands Benefits for Tourism Business and Hospitality Sector
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced new support measures for tourism entrepreneurs, including expanded preferential lending for hotel construction and renovation. The duration of subsidies for three-, four-, and five-star hotels has been extended. Tax benefits for property and land taxes have also been prolonged for hotels and campsites.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Unify Banks into a Single Faster Payment System
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan is developing a Faster Payment System (FPS) to enable real-time money transfers 24/7 between individuals and legal entities, regardless of their bank. The system aims to unify various payment systems and ensure interoperability. Transfers will be possible using a single recipient identifier, such as a phone number or QR code.

item.title: US Suspends Global Immigration Visa Processing for Enhanced Vetting
item.description: The Trump administration has halted global immigration visa processing for additional training of consular staff. This aims to better vet applicants and identify those potentially reliant on US public benefits. Interviews are being rescheduled indefinitely, with no resumption date announced.

item.title: Tajikistan National Bank Launches Three-Month Pilot for Digital Tax System for Individuals
item.description: Tajikistan's National Bank has initiated a three-month pilot phase for a digital platform aimed at improving tax administration for individual entrepreneurs. The system, developed with the Agency of Innovations and Digital Technologies, seeks to simplify reporting and reduce administrative burdens.

item.title: Ala-Archa glacier loses 1.4 meters of ice in one month
item.description: An expedition to Ala-Archa Gorge recorded approximately 1.4 meters of ice melt near the glacier's tongue in just one month. Scientists installed ablation rods to measure melting intensity and glacier surface changes. Active melting occurs from May to September, with lower areas potentially losing 4-5 meters over the season.

item.title: India expects "significant progress" in mining cooperation with Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan and India have signed a memorandum on cooperation in mining and geological resources, intending to implement it. India's Ministry of External Affairs representative Sibi George stated that commercial project implementation and delegation exchanges are being discussed. India is interested in attracting its companies to develop promising Uzbek deposits.

item.title: Iranian President's plane makes emergency landing in Rasht returning from Bishkek
item.description: The plane carrying Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, returning from Kyrgyzstan after the SCO summit, made an unscheduled landing in Rasht instead of Tehran. Reports suggest the landing might have been prompted by air defense system activation in Tehran, though no official confirmation exists.

item.title: SCO Summit in Bishkek Signals Clear Message of Multipolar World Order
item.description: The SCO summit in Bishkek sent a clear signal to Western powers about the multipolar nature of the global order. The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation is strengthening its position as an alternative model to the US-dominated international system. The presence of leaders from China, Russia, India, and Turkey highlighted this shift.

item.title: Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region's energy capacity reaches 70 MW
item.description: The energy capacity of Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region has significantly increased over 34 years, reaching 70 MW by 2025, up from 10.4 MW in 1991. Several state investment projects totaling over 700 million somoni were implemented. The number of power plants grew from 13 (44 MW) in 2021 to 36 by 2026.

item.title: Road repairs in Naryn continue, Ministry of Transport responds to deputy
item.description: Road repairs in Naryn, Kyrgyzstan, are ongoing, according to the Ministry of Transport and Communications. The ministry refuted claims by a deputy that work had stopped and equipment removed, stating that 9.025 km of road base and asphalt layers are complete, with road markings applied to 70% of the section. Bridge repairs are finished.

item.title: Bank of Georgia owner considers acquiring major Uzbek bank
item.description: Lion Finance Group, owner of Bank of Georgia, is exploring the possibility of entering the Uzbek banking market by acquiring a leading local bank. The group's CEO, Archil Gachechiladze, stated they are focusing on top three or five players, aiming to replicate Bank of Georgia's digital model in new markets. Specific banks under consideration were not disclosed.

item.title: First liver and kidney transplant surgeries performed in Khujand
item.description: The first liver and kidney transplant surgeries in the Sogd region were successfully completed without complications at Clinical Hospital No. 1 in Khujand. The operations were performed by specialists from the National Scientific Center for Organ and Human Tissue Transplantation in collaboration with Khujand hospital surgeons. Patient conditions are stable.

item.title: Nearly 16,000 Indian students studying in Uzbekistan, says Indian MFA
item.description: Approximately 16,000 Indian students are currently studying in Uzbekistan, primarily in medical fields, according to India's Ministry of External Affairs. Following talks between Presidents Mirziyoyev and Modi, both countries agreed to expand educational cooperation, including student exchanges and joint research. India also proposed attracting foreign university campuses to its GIFT City financial hub.

item.title: India's UPI Payment System May Launch in Uzbekistan in About a Year
item.description: India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) system could become operational in Uzbekistan in approximately one year, following a network agreement between NPCI International Payments Limited and Uzbekistan's HUMO payment system. This collaboration aims to enable UPI payments across Uzbekistan via the UzQR national QR network.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India nearing long-term uranium supply deal
item.description: Uzbekistan and India are close to signing a new long-term agreement for uranium supply. Discussions were positive, according to India's Ministry of External Affairs. Both countries also agreed to explore cooperation in geology, mining, and peaceful nuclear energy.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Praised for Excellent SCO Chairmanship Performance
item.description: SCO Secretary-General Nurlan Yermekbayev stated Kyrgyzstan performed excellently as the chairing state of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation. He noted the country managed both leading the organization and organizing events for its 25th anniversary. Kyrgyzstan hosted over 200 events during its chairmanship, launching mechanisms for various specialized meetings.

item.title: SCO Summit Focuses on Multipolar World and Global Governance Reform
item.description: The 25th SCO summit addressed strengthening the UN's role and forming a multipolar world, aligning with the SCO's goals for global governance reform. The speech highlighted the irreversible historical process of multipolar world formation, driven by the Global South's growth, and advocated for an equitable and orderly multipolar world.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Unifying Banks into a Single Fast Payment System
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank has proposed a new regulation for a fast payment system. This system aims to enable individuals and businesses to send money in real-time, 24/7, regardless of their bank. The project seeks to create unified rules and connect various financial institutions for interoperability.

item.title: SCO Reiterates Call for Taliban to Form Inclusive Government in Afghanistan
item.description: Leaders of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) at their summit in Bishkek reiterated their call for the Taliban to form an inclusive government in Afghanistan. They stated that such a government is the only path to lasting peace, involving all ethnic and political groups. The SCO reaffirmed its commitment to a peaceful, neutral Afghanistan free from terrorism and drugs.

item.title: US and Iran exchange accusations over massive strikes
item.description: The United States Central Command reported the successful completion of strikes on Iranian military targets, including IRGC facilities. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated the US attack on a residential building killed and wounded over 50 civilians. Tehran also claimed retaliatory attacks on bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Iraqi Kurdistan, and stated that many US soldiers died in an attack on Jordan.

item.title: Certain customs requirements to be canceled, export fees to decrease by 30%
item.description: Uzbekistan will introduce new regulations to simplify customs procedures and enhance convenience for entrepreneurs. Starting September 1, 2026, restrictions on advance payments for imports based on invoices without foreign trade contracts will be lifted. Requirements for advance payment security for exports, including national currency transactions, will also be removed.

item.title: Official meeting between Sadyr Japarov and Shehbaz Sharif held in Bishkek
item.description: An official meeting took place in Bishkek between Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who is on an official visit. Japarov emphasized Kyrgyzstan's view of Pakistan as a reliable partner in South Asia. The leaders noted the transition from political dialogue to practical cooperation and planned to sign several documents.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Sentenced to Three Years for Fighting in Russia-Ukraine War
item.description: A court in Uzbekistan's Xorazm region sentenced citizen Z.Yu. to three years in prison for fighting on the Russian side in the Russia-Ukraine war. Z.Yu. was recruited in Ufa, Bashkortostan, and received military training before being deployed to Donetsk Oblast.

item.title: Zafarabad District Governor Injured in Road Accident
item.description: The governor of Zafarabad district in Jizzakh region, Gayratjon Eshpo'latov, was involved in a road accident while in his official vehicle. Two people were in the car. The governor's condition is reported as serious.

item.title: Kyrgyz farmers sell fallen apples for low prices due to processing shortage
item.description: Farmers in Batken region, Kyrgyzstan, are selling fallen apples for 3 soms per kilogram due to a lack of processing facilities. Some apples fall from trees due to disease, affecting about 10 percent of orchards. Local residents resell these apples to Uzbekistan, where processing is more developed. Farmers have advocated for processing plants and cold storage for 20 years.

item.title: Xi Jinping attends SCO+ meeting, calls for equitable multipolar world
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping attended an SCO+ meeting, advocating for an equitable and orderly multipolar world and improved global governance. He stated that hegemonism and unilateralism are acting against historical trends, while the global majority seeks a dignified place through development and cooperation. The rise of the Global South, he noted, has made multipolarity an irreversible historical process.

item.title: Two individuals arrested in Tashkent for allegedly selling Uzbek entry visas for $31,000
item.description: Two people have been arrested in Tashkent for allegedly arranging Uzbek entry visas for foreigners for a fee. A 41-year-old man was detained while receiving $31,200 from three foreigners. He reportedly intended to give $27,000 to a 66-year-old accomplice, who was also apprehended. Criminal proceedings have been initiated.

item.title: Two individuals arrested in Tashkent for extorting $31,200 for Uzbek visas
item.description: Two people were apprehended in Tashkent for illegally obtaining $31,200 from foreign citizens in exchange for Uzbek entry visas. One individual facilitated visas for three foreigners through acquaintances, keeping $4,200 and giving $27,000 to their accomplice.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament Speaker to investigate MPs' alleged involvement in land transfer to foreigners
item.description: The Speaker of the Kyrgyz Parliament, Marlen Mamataliev, will investigate allegations of parliamentary deputies' involvement in granting land to foreign entities. He stated that no law allowing land sales to China has been passed, but existing legislation permits long-term land use. New draft laws aim to strengthen restrictions on land allocation.

item.title: Zafarobod District Governor Hospitalized After Traffic Accident
item.description: The governor of Zafarobod district in Jizzakh region, Gayratjon Eshpolatov, was hospitalized in intensive care after a traffic accident involving his official car and a truck. The incident occurred on August 30. A criminal case has been initiated. The governor's son, who was driving, also sustained injuries.

item.title: Uzbekistan Imposes Three-Year Moratorium on Small Business Inspections
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has decreed a three-year moratorium on inspections of small businesses, effective August 27, 2026. Exceptions include inspections related to criminal cases, health impacts, labor law compliance, and specific citizen appeals. The Business Ombudsman will review past inspections.

item.title: New Water Supply Line in Zafarabad to Serve 400 Families
item.description: New water supply facilities have been launched in Zafarabad district, Sughd region, Tajikistan. A new drinking water line in the village of Bahoriston will initially provide clean water to 400 families, addressing long-standing water access issues. The project aims to improve living conditions and public health.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon inaugurates new school for 800 students in Dushanbe
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon opened the new 'Imkon' non-state school in Dushanbe on September 2, 2026. The facility, built by entrepreneurs, accommodates 800 students and features modern classrooms, labs, sports facilities, and swimming pools. The school emphasizes domestic materials and local employment.

item.title: Putin: Russia is winning on the battlefield, no negotiations with terrorists
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that Russia is winning on the battlefield and that negotiations with terrorists will not occur. He asserted that the enemy would soon surrender and denied reports of a new military mobilization in Russia.

item.title: Physical Abuse of Children at Andijan Care Center Revealed; Seven Staff Fired
item.description: Physical abuse of children has been identified at the "G'amxo'rlik" center in Andijan, leading to the dismissal of seven staff members. Disciplinary measures were also taken against officials who failed to adequately supervise the educators' work. Further details are available online.
